title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the previous page: S is a connected scheme over Q, s̄ a geometric point, A an abelian group, and ξ: A → G_m(S) a homomorphism. E_∞(ξ) is the 'Kummer' object whose fibre at s̄ consists of compatible systems of n-th roots of the units ξ(a), for all n. That fibre is an extension (342):
 1 → T → E_∞(ξ)_s̄ → A → 1, with T = T_∞(k̄*) ≅ Ẑ(1).
π_1(S,s̄) acts on this fibre (map (341)). It acts trivially on A and through the cyclotomic character χ on T.

The group G (344) consists of the automorphisms u of the extension that induce the identity on A and a homothety μ ∈ Ẑ* on T. This gives an exact sequence 1 → Hom_Z(A,T) → G → Ẑ*.

On this page:
(i) The image of G → Ẑ* consists of the μ for which the push-out of (342) by the homothety μ_T has the same class in Ext(A,T).
(ii) The action (341) is therefore a homomorphism ρ_ξ: π_1 → G whose composite with G → Ẑ* is the cyclotomic character (diagram (346)).
(iii) If S is of finite type over Q, the image of the cyclotomic character is open. The reason: a closed point has a number field as residue field, and the cyclotomic character of a number field has open image. Hence the image of G → Ẑ* is a fortiori open.
(iv) The image of G → Ẑ* is all of Ẑ* if the cyclotomic character is surjective. He glosses this as 'i.e. if the only roots of unity on S are ±1', e.g. S = Spec Q.
(v) Diagram (346) is functorial in A; the next page uses this to reduce the study of Im ρ_ξ to simpler A.

In modern terms, ρ_ξ is the profinite Kummer representation attached to a group of units, with values in Hom(A,Ẑ(1)) ⋊ Ẑ*. The page is part of computing its image, i.e. a Bashmakov/Ribet-type open-image question, inside the Longue Marche study of Galois actions on fundamental groups.
errors: The 'i.e.' equating surjectivity of the cyclotomic character on π_1(S) with 'the only roots of unity on S are ±1' is wrong as stated. Counterexample: S = Spec Q(√2) has only ±1 as roots of unity, yet its cyclotomic character has index 2 because √2 ∈ Q(ζ_8). Surjectivity requires the field of constants to be linearly disjoint from Q(μ_∞).

The weaker condition (μ(S) = {±1}) does suffice for surjectivity of G → Ẑ*, by a different route. The extension class (342) is governed by ξ restricted to A_tors, which takes values in μ(S) = {±1}, and every μ ∈ Ẑ* acts trivially on ±1. So the conclusion about G is right, but it does not follow via π_1 as written.
Equation numbering is inconsistent: the diagram on this page is labelled (345) like the exact sequence on the previous page, while the text and the next page call it (346).

ideas.what: The automorphism group G of the Kummer extension 1→Ẑ(1)→E→A→1, sitting in 1→Hom(A,Ẑ(1))→G→Ẑ*; its image in Ẑ* is the stabiliser of the extension class.
ideas.modern_name: Group of the Kummer representation, Hom(A,Ẑ(1)) ⋊ Ẑ* (affine group of the Kummer tower)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical Kummer theory; Bashmakov (1960s-70s), Ribet (1979), Bertrand
ideas.where_published: Possibly implicit in La Longue Marche discussions of Kummer torsors; not certain

ideas.what: The Galois/π_1 action on the Kummer extension factors through G, compatibly with the cyclotomic character.
ideas.modern_name: Kummer representation ρ_ξ: π_1(S) → Hom(A,Ẑ(1)) ⋊ Ẑ*

ideas.what: Openness of the cyclotomic image for S of finite type over Q, hence of the image of G in Ẑ*.
ideas.modern_name: Open image of the cyclotomic character over finitely generated fields

ideas.what: Functoriality of the diagram in A, used to reduce the image computation to simpler A.

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine set-up of profinite Kummer theory: the image of Galois in Hom(A,Ẑ(1)) ⋊ Ẑ* and its open image in Ẑ*. It is well established in the literature (Bashmakov, Ribet), and the page contains a minor sloppy equivalence about roots of unity.
transcription_corrections: The insertion above μ_T reads 'l'homothétie' (i.e. 'telles que l'homothétie μ_T ne change pas la classe'), not 'à l'iso. près'.
The label on the vertical arrow π_1 → G is ρ_ξ (cf. next page), not χ_ξ. The annotation reads roughly 'comm.', with 'caractère cyclotomique' attached to the diagonal π_1 → Ẑ*.
The text says 'Le diagramme (346)'; the diagram itself is labelled ambiguously, (345) or (346).
The coefficient group is written T_∞(k̄*) (lowercase k̄ as on the previous page), not T_∞(K̄*).
